(اختار): the alif in it is changed from a yāʾ; its origin is اختير with fatḥa on the yāʾ, because the maṣdar is اختيار, where the yāʾ returned to its origin; when the yāʾ was voweled after a fatḥa it was changed into an alif. Its pattern is افتعل.
(الغافرين): plural of الغافر, an active participle of the triliteral غفر; its pattern is فاعل.
(هدنا): in it there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, to suit indeclinability on sukūn. It is a hollow weak verb, هاد يهود, meaning to return; its origin is هودنا. When the dāl was made indeclinable on sukūn and two vowelless letters met, the weak letter was deleted. Its pattern is فلنا.
(الأمّيّ): see a discussion of the morphology of this word at ayah (78) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(مكتوبا): a passive participle of the triliteral كتب, on the pattern مفعول.
(الخبائث): plural of خبيثة, the feminine of خبيث, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the verb خبث يخبث, of the bāb karuma; its pattern is فعيل, and the pattern of الخبائث is فعائل. The yāʾ was changed into a hamza because it is preceded by a vowelless alif, and it is additional.
(الأغلال): plural of غلّ, a primitive (jāmid) noun for that with which one is shackled, used metaphorically here for hardship; its pattern is فعل, with kasra on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
- In this ayah there is an explicit indication that the Torah and the Gospel explicitly gave glad tidings of the mission of Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. But the Jews used to distort words from their places, to obliterate that glad tiding, and the distortion of the words was either by passing over some of what came in the Torah and concealing it, or by interpreting it in a way different from what was intended; and both were done by the Jews of Medina and Khaybar and those of their ilk.

safi-cedvel:195-195.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for rhetorical-denial interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (أرجل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (يمشون) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يمشون), (أم) it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, conveying digression (iḍrāb); (لهم أيد يبطشون بها) like لهم أرجل يمشون بها, and the sign of the nominative in أيد is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the nunation, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (أم لهم ...
يسمعون بها) like أم لهم أيد ... and (أم) in the three places means بل («rather»), and the hamza is for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī).
The clause «لهم أرجل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يمشون بها» is in the position of the nominative as naʿt (adjective) of أجل [Translator's note: so in the source; أرجل is evidently meant.].
The clause «لهم أيد ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يبطشون بها» is in the position of the nominative as naʿt of أيد.
The clause «لهم أعين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يبصرون بها» is in the position of the nominative as naʿt of أعين.
The clause «لهم آذان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يسمعون بها» is in the position of the nominative as naʿt of آذان.
(قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «you» (أنت); (ادعوا) like the preceding one (1), (شركاء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (كيدوا) like ادعوا (2), and (النون) is for protection (al-wiqāya) and (الياء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) a conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-making; (تنظروا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (النون) is for protection, and the dropped (الياء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ادعوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of saying).
The clause «كيدون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause ادعوا.
The clause «لا تنظرون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كيدون.

* Morphology:
«يمشون»: it contains a weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion. Its origin is يمشيون – with ḍamma on the second yāʾ –; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was moved to the shīn and the yāʾ was made quiescent; then two sukūns met: the yāʾ and the wāw, so the yāʾ was deleted and it became يمشون; its pattern is يفعون.
(أيد): plural of يد; its origin is أيدي. The yāʾ was deleted in keeping with the nunation, because it is a defective noun; its pattern is أفع.. The nunation here is the nunation of compensation (tanwīn ʿiwaḍ), not the nunation of full declinability (tanwīn tamkīn).

* Rhetoric:
1- In the saying of Allah the Exalted (أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِها) up to His saying «فَلا تُنْظِرُونِ» there is a figure of embellishment (badīʿ) known as «negating a thing by affirming it» (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābihi). It is that the speaker affirms something in the outward sense of his speech, on condition that the affirmed thing is borrowed, then negates figuratively what belongs to its cause; and what is truly negated in the inner sense of the speech is what he affirmed, not what he negated. In the preceding verses it entails negating divinity altogether from those of the gods taken besides Allah the Exalted that see and hear – so how much more from those of them that neither hear nor see.

* Benefits:
1- Coordinating conjunction (ʿaṭf al-nasaq): it is a follower between which and the word it follows one of the conjunctions comes.
Its kinds are three:
a- conjunction on the wording (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-lafẓ) b- conjunction on the position (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-maḥall) c- conjunction on supposition (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum) 2- The conjunctions are «eleven, namely: الواو، الفاء، ثم، حتى، أم، أو، لكن، بل، لا، لا يكون، ليس». The basic rule is that conjoining is to the first, except with the particles of sequence ...
3- The conjunctions are of two kinds:
a- those that entail sharing in wording and meaning absolutely, and they are four: «الواو، الفاء، ثم، حتى».
b- those that entail sharing in wording but not in meaning:
either because it affirms for what follows it a ruling that is negated of what precedes it, namely بل and لكن; or because it is the reverse, namely «لا and ليس». We have detailed this discussion in another place, so let whoever seeks it return to it.

safi-cedvel:196-196.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (وليّي) ism of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty; (نزّل) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is «he»; (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (يتولّى) imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is «he»; (الصالحين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «إنّ وليّي الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «نزّل الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «هو يتولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «يتولّى الصالحين» is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هو.

safi-cedvel:197-197.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تدعون من دونه) the i'rab of its like has passed [Note: In verse (194) of this sūra.]; (لا) a negative particle; (يستطيعون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (نصر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (لا أنفسهم ينصرون) like لا يستطيعون نصركم, with the object fronted.
The clause «الذين تدعون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ وليّي الله [Note: In the previous verse (196).].
The clause «تدعون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا يستطيعون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «ينصرون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يستطيعون.

safi-cedvel:198-198.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunctive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (تدعو) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلى الهدى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تدعوهم), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (لا) negative; (يسمعوا) imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunctive; (ترى) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «you» (أنت), and (هم) like the previous; (ينظرون) like يستطيعون (1), (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينظرون), (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لا يبصرون) like لا يستطيعون (2).
The clause «تدعوهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause الذين تدعون (3).
The clause «لا يسمعوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تراهم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تدعوهم.
The clause «ينظرون ...» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (تراهم).
The clause «هم لا يبصرون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the subject pronoun in (ينظرون).
The clause «لا يبصرون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هم.

safi-cedvel:113-114.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (جاء) a past verb. (السحرة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (فرعون) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and it is prevented from nunation for being a proper name and foreign. (قالوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh). (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). (اللام) for emphasis. (أجرا) the noun of inna, postponed, accusative. (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle. (كنّا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative, the noun of kāna. (نحن) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun (نا).], (الغالبين) the khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «جاء السحرة ... » is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with (قد) implied.].
And the clause: «إنّ لنا لأجرا ... » is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).
And the clause: «إن كنّا نحن الغالبين» has no grammatical position, resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: فهل لنا أجر.
(قال) like جاء, and the fāʿil is هو. (نعم) a particle of answer. (الواو) a conjunction. (إن) like the first, and (كم) a pronoun, the noun of inna. (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (من المقرّبين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of inna.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the implied clause after the particle of answer is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl, i.e. نعم إنّكم مأجورون.
And the clause: «إنّكم لمن المقرّبين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.

* Morphology:
(السحرة): plural of ساحر, an active participle whose pattern is فاعل, from the triliteral سحر.. and the pattern of السحرة is فعلة with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:115-116.t:
* I'rab:
(قالوا) like the previous one [Note: in ayah (113) of this surah.], (يا) a vocative particle. (موسى) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, in the position of accusative. (إمّا) a particle of choice (takhyīr). (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle. (تلقي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil (agent) is أنت.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تلقي) is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being مبدوء به («is begun with») [Note: Or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: اختر إلقاءك.].
(الواو) a conjunction. (إمّا) like the first. (أن نكون) like أن تلقي; the verb is defective, an abrogator (nāsikh), and its noun is نحن. (نحن الملقين) like نحن الغالبين [Note: in ayah (113) of this surah.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نكون..) is like the first interpreted maṣdar.
The clause: «قالوا ... » is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «the vocative and its complement ... » is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).
And the clause: «إلقاؤك (مبدوء به) » has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «تلقي ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
And the clause: «كون إلقائنا (مبدوء به) » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
And the clause: «نكون ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is هو. (ألقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الفاء) a conjunction. (لمّا) an adverb meaning «when» (حين), indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the answer سحروا. (ألقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (سحروا) like قالوا «1», (أعين) mafʿūl bihi. (الواو) a conjunction. (جاؤوا) like قالوا «2».
(بسحر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاؤوا) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of جاؤوا.], (عظيم) naʿt (adjective) of سحر, genitive.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
And the clause: «ألقوا» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «ألقوا — with fatḥa on the qāf —» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
And the clause: «سحروا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «استرهبوهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سحروا.
And the clause: «جاؤوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause سحروا.

* Morphology:
(الملقين): plural of الملقي, an active participle from the quadriliteral ألقى; its pattern is المفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: two quiescent yāʾs came together, so the yāʾ that is the lām of the word was deleted to escape the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the pattern of الملقين is مفعين, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).
(ألقوا): it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its origin is ألقيوا. The yāʾ came with ḍamma, and the vowel was felt heavy on it, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the qāf before it — iʿlāl by quiescence — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it became ألقوا; its pattern is أفعوا.

safi-cedvel:117-122.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (أوحينا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil (agent). (إلى موسى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحينا); the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, a diptote. (أن) a particle of explanation (tafsīr). (ألق) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (عصا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) a conjunction. (إذا) of surprise, with no grammatical position. (هي) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (تلقف) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi [Note: Some allowed (ما) to be maṣdar-forming, but this is far-fetched, for how could the swallowing of the falsehood take place when it is] [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.], (يأفكون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. يأفكونه.
The clause: «أوحينا ... » is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause ألق ... has no grammatical position, explicative.
And the clause هي تلقف ... has no grammatical position, conjoined to an omitted clause, the implied wording being فألقاها فإذا هي تلقف.. and the omitted clause has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أوحينا.
And the clause: «تلقف ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ هي.
And the clause: «يأفكون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
(الفاء) a conjunction. (وقع) a past verb. (الحقّ) fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) a conjunction. (بطل) like وقع. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil of بطل.], (كانوا) a defective past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (يعملون) like يأفكون.
And the clause: «وقع الحقّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause هي تلقف.
And the clause: «بطل ما ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause وقع الحقّ.
And the clause: «كانوا يعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «يعملون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
(الفاء) a conjunction. (غلبوا) a passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.
and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (هنالك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (غلبوا); (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address. (الواو) a conjunction. (انقلبوا) a past verb with its fāʿil. (صاغرين) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil of انقلبوا, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «غلبوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause بطل..
And the clause: «انقلبوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause غلبوا.
(الواو) a conjunction! (ألقي) a passive past verb. (السحرة) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (ساجدين) a ḥāl, accusative, from the nāʾib fāʿil, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «القي السحرة» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause انقلبوا.
(قالوا) like انقلبوا. (آمنّا) like أوحينا. (برت) [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for «بربّ».] a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنّا). (العالمين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil السحرة, with (قد) implied, or from the pronoun in ساجدين.].
And the clause: «آمنّا ... » is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).
(ربّ) a badal (substitute) for the first ربّ, genitive [Note: Or it is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) for ربّ; and al-Jamal allowed it to be a naʿt (adjective) of ربّ العالمين.], (موسى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa implied on the alif, a diptote. (الواو) a conjunction. (هارون) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to موسى, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote, for being a proper name and foreign.

* Morphology:
(ألق): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion to suit the indeclinable form, for it is the imperative of the weak verb يلقي; its pattern is أفع.
(هارون): see ayah (248) of Surat al-Baqara.

* Benefits:
- The art of the Quranic story is an art different from the art of the story, old and modern. On the one hand it takes the path of dialogue, and it takes up the important points of the story and leaves aside what is below that. But the reader and listener read between the lines, «as is said», and so grasp the course of the story from its beginning to its end.

safi-cedvel:123-124.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb. (فرعون) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (آمنتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; an interrogative hamza before it is omitted, and it is for disapproval and rebuke. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle [Translator's note: the source text appears to be missing words here; it evidently intended «(الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to آمنتم; (قبل) … (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle». It is translated as written.] (آذن) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا. (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آذن). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh). (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis. (مكر) khabar (predicate), nominative. (مكرتم) like آمنتم, and (الواو) is redundant (zāʾida), a lengthening of the vowel of the mīm, and (الهاء) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (في المدينة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of مكرتم [Note: Or it is attached to (مكرتموه).], (اللام) the lām of consequence, or for causation — (اخرجوا) [Translator's note: so in the source, for «تخرجوا».] an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (منها) like به, attached to (تخرجوا). (أهل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تخرجوا..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (مكرتموه). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition. (سوف) a particle for the future. (تعلمون) like يعملون [Note: in ayah (118) of this surah.]; the object of تعلمون is implied, i.e. the consequence of your deed.
The clause: «قال فرعون ... » is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنتم به» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).
And the clause: «آذن لكم ... » has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن), and the interpreted maṣdar (أن آذن..) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «إنّ هذا لمكر ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) within the scope of Pharaoh's speech.
And the clause: «مكرتموه» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of مكر.
And the clause: «سوف تعلمون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن فعلتم فسوف تعلمون ...
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (أقطعنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative because it is free of any accusative or jussive governor.. and (النّون) is the nūn of emphasis, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being أنا. (أيدي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (أرجلكم) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أيدي, accusative.. and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi. (من خلاف) a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (ثمّ) a conjunction. (لأصلّبنّ) like لأقطّعنّ, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (أجمعين) a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached accusative pronoun, following it in the accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «اقطّعنّ ... » has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath; the oath and its answer are an explanation of the preceding threat [Note: Or an explanatory resumption.].
And the clause: «أصلّبنّكم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer-of-the-oath clause with the repetition of the lām [Note: Or it is the answer to another implied oath, and the oath clause is conjoined to the first oath clause.].

* Morphology:
(آذن): the long vowel in it is originally two hamzas, the first being the hamza of the imperfect, vowelled with fatḥa, and the second an original quiescent one, i.e. أأذن; the well-known rule is that the two hamzas are changed into a madda over a single alif.
(المدينة): a primitive (jāmid) noun whose pattern is فعلية [Translator's note: so in the source; the pattern is فعيلة.]; its plural is مدن on the measure فعل with two ḍammas, and مدائن on the measure فعائل.

safi-cedvel:26-26.t:
* I'rab:
(يا): a vocative particle. (بني): the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, treated like the sound masculine plural (mulḥaq bi-jamʿ al-mudhakkar). (آدم): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, a diptote. (قد): a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (أنزلنا): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn ... (ونا) is a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent), for majesty (taʿẓīm). (على): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزلنا). (لباسا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (يواري): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ. (سوءات): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): a conjunction. (ريشا): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to لباس, accusative like it, and it stands in for an omitted qualified noun, i.e. «لباسا ريشا» ("a garment of plumage"), i.e. adornment. (الواو): resumptive. (لباس): mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (التقوى): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif. (ذلك): a demonstrative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ [Note: Or badal (substitute) from لباس التقوى, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to it, and (خير) is the khabar (predicate) of لباس.]. And (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (خير): the khabar of the demonstrative, nominative. (ذلك): like the first. (من آيات): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك. (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لعلّ): a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), for hope (tarajjī) — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the ism (subject) of laʿalla. (يذّكّرون): an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The vocative clause «يا بني ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «قد أنزلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, the reply to the vocative.
The clause «يواري ...»: in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of (لباسا).
The clause «لباس التقوى ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ذلك خير»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (لباس التقوى).
The clause «ذلك من آيات الله»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لعلّهم يذّكّرون»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «يذّكّرون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.

* Morphology:
(ريشا): a noun for what grows on a bird, or it is a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb راش يريش, i.e. he put feathers on it; and it may bear both senses at one and the same time. Its pattern is فِعْل, with kasra then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى». Its like occurs frequently in the speech of poets, among it:
إذا المرء لم يلبس لباسا من التقى ... تقلب عريانا وإن كان كاسيا
(When a man does not wear a garment of piety, he turns about naked even if he is clothed.)

safi-cedvel:27-27.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بني آدم): like the first [Note: In the previous āya (26).]. (لا): prohibitive, causing the jussive. (يفتننّ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm), and (النون) is for emphasis, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الشيطان): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (الكاف): a preposition of comparison (tashbīh). (ما): a maṣdar-forming particle. (أخرج): a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو). (أبوي): mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (من الجنّة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخرج).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أخرج) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, with a muḍāf omitted, attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is يفتننّكم, i.e.: «فتنة كفتنة إخراج أبويكم ...» ("a trial like the trial of expelling your two parents ...").
(ينزع): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو). (عن): a preposition, and (هما) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (ينزع). (لباس): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام): for cause (taʿlīl). (يري): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām, and (هما) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو). (سوءات): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (هما) is muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يريهما) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (ينزع).
(إنّ: a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the ism (subject) of inna. (يرى): an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (هو): a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun. (الواو): a conjunction. (قبيل): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the latent pronoun that is the fāʿil of يرى, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من): a preposition. (حيث): a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (يراكم). (لا): negative. (ترون): an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (إنّا): like أنّه. (جعلنا): a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ...
(ونا) is the fāʿil. (الشياطين): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (أولياء): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is prevented from nunation because it is assimilated to the noun ending in the extended feminine alif (alif al-taʾnīth al-mamdūda). (اللام): a preposition. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to أولياء. (لا): negative. (يؤمنون): like ترون ...
The clause «يا بني آدم..»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «لا يفتننّكم الشيطان»: has no grammatical position, the reply to the vocative.
The clause «أخرج أبويكم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «ينزع..»: in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from أبويكم, i.e. «منزوعا عنهما لباسهما» ("their garment having been stripped from them"), or from the agent pronoun in (أخرج), i.e. «نازعا عنهما لباسهما» ("stripping their garment from them").
The clause «يريهما ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّه يراكم ...»: has no grammatical position, a cause (taʿlīl) for the prohibition in His saying: لا يفتننّكم.
The clause «يراكم ...»: in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna.
[Translator's note: The source writes «أنّ» here; the particle in the āya is «إنّ».]
The clause «لا ترونهم»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنا جعلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, another cause for the prohibition.
The clause «جعلنا ...»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the second inna.
The clause «لا يؤمنون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).

* Morphology:
(قبيل): a noun for a group consisting of three or more; القبيلة is not the feminine of القبيل. Its plural is قُبُل, with two ḍammas. In al-Miṣbāḥ: القبيلة is a dialectal variant of القبيل. Its pattern is فعيل.

* Benefits:
1- Dialogue in the Noble Quran:
Attention has already been drawn to this characteristic among the characteristics of the Quran, namely dialogue. It most often takes place between partners in conversation, and its material is "saying" (al-qawl). It is an original method which the Quran adopted as a means for narratives and for presenting reports, for it is more conducive to understanding and stronger in effect; and to Allah belongs the far-reaching wisdom..
2- The links (rawābiṭ) of the khabar to the mubtadaʾ (subject), when it is a clause, are four:
a- An overt or latent pronoun, as in «الظلم مرتعه وخيم» ("Injustice — its pasture is unwholesome").
b- Pointing to it, as in «وَلِباسُ التَّقْوى ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ».
c- Repeating the mubtadaʾ with its own wording, as in «الْحَاقَّةُ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ». d- Generality (ʿumūm), as in «خالد نعم الرجل» ("Khālid — how excellent the man!").
So خالد is the mubtadaʾ, the clause نعم is its khabar, and the link is generality.

safi-cedvel:28-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قالوا). (فعلوا): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (فاحشة): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (قالوا): like فعلوا. (وجدنا): a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. (ونا) is the fāʿil. (على): a preposition, and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from آباء [Note: This is if the verb is transitive to one object ... and it is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi if the verb is transitive to two.], i.e. «عاكفين عليها» ("devoted to it"). (آباء): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو): a conjunction. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (أمر): a past verb, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو), and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الباء): a preposition, and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أمر). (قل): an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you" (أنت). (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl) — abrogating (nāsikh). (الله): the Name of Majesty, the ism (subject) of inna, accusative. (لا): negative. (يأمر): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو). (بالفحشاء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأمر). (الهمزة): for disapproving, rebuking interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-tawbīkhī). (تقولون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (على الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقلون) [Translator's note: so printed; read (تقولون).], through its being made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of «تتقوّلون» ("you falsely attribute"). (ما): a relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), and the clause after it is a naʿt (adjective) of it ... As for the referent (ʿāʾid), it is omitted in both kinds, i.e.:
«تعلمونه» ("you know it").], indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (لا): negative. (تعلمون): like تقولون.
The clause «فعلوا....»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالوا....»: has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «وجدنا ...»: in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «الله أمرنا بها»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أمرنا....»: in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «قل....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يأمر....»: in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «لا يأمر بالفحشاء»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «تقولون....»: has no grammatical position, a resumption (istiʾnāf) falling within the scope of the saying.
The clause «لا تعلمون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).

safi-cedvel:29-30.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت). (أمر): a past verb. (ربّ): fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (بالقسط): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أمر). (الواو): a conjunction. (أقيموا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (وجوه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (عند): an adverb, accusative, attached to (أقيموا). (كلّ): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (مسجد): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): a conjunction. (ادعوا): like أقيموا, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (مخلصين): ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the fāʿil of ادعوه, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ. (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to مخلصين. (الدين): mafʿūl bihi of the active participle, accusative. (الكاف): a preposition of comparison (tashbīh). (ما): a maṣdar-forming particle. (بدأ): a past verb, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما بدأكم) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is the following verb, i.e.: «تعودون عودا كبدء خلقكم» ("you will return a return like the beginning of your creation").
(تعودون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قل....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أمر ربّي....»: in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «أقيموا....»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the content of the clause of maqūl al-qawl [Note: Because His saying أمر ربّى بالقسط means «أقسطوا» ("act justly"); so the clause of maqūl al-qawl is declarative (khabariyya) in wording and performative (inshāʾiyya) in meaning, and so it is valid to conjoin the clause أقيموا to it.. It is also permissible to conjoin the clause أقيموا to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative taken from the maṣdar (القسط), because the meaning is: «أمر ربّي بأن أقسطوا وأقيموا» ("my Lord has commanded that you act justly and set ...")..].
The clause «ادعوه»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause أقيموا.
The clause «بدأكم ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «تعودون»: has no grammatical position, a resumption containing the sense of cause (taʿlīl) for the command أقيموا.
(30) (فريقا): a fronted mafʿūl bihi [Note: Or a ḥāl, accusative, from the fāʿil of تعودون, i.e. «تعودون فريقا مهديّا» ("you return as a guided party"), and the clause after it is a naʿt (adjective) of it.], accusative, its governor being هدى. (هدى): a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو), i.e. Allah. (الواو): a conjunction. (فريقا): mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أضلّ" ("He led astray"). (حق): a past verb. (على): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (حقّ). (الضلالة): fāʿil, nominative [Note: The fāʿil came with the verb in the masculine because the feminine fāʿil (الضلالة) is figuratively feminine (muʾannath majāzī).]. (إنّهم اتّخذوا الشياطين): like إنّه يراكم [Note: In āya (27) of this sura.]. (أولياء): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and it is prevented from nunation because it is assimilated to the noun ending in the extended feminine alif (alif al-taʾnīth al-mamdūda). (من دون): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of أولياء. (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): a conjunction. (يحسبون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (أنّ): a particle resembling the verb (ḥarf mushabbah bi-l-fiʿl), for emphasis — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the ism (subject) of anna. (مهتدون): the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم مهتدون) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسبون.
The clause «هدى....»: has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: It may be in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the fāʿil of بدأ, who is Allah, with قد implied.].
The clause «حقّ عليهم الضلالة»: conjoined to the clause هدى, taking its i'rab.
The clause «إنّهم اتّخذوا»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «اتّخذوا....»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يحسبون....»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause اتّخذوا [Note: It may be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هم, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of اتّخذوا.].

* Morphology:
(مسجد): a noun of place from the triliteral سجد, of the bāb of نصر; its pattern is مفعِل with kasra on the ʿayn, contrary to analogy (qiyās), for by analogy the ʿayn would have fatḥa, since it has ḍamma on the ʿayn in the imperfect.... It may also be a mīmī maṣdar, likewise contrary to analogy.

* Rhetoric:
1- Simile (tashbīh): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «كَما بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ», where He, glory be to Him, likened the restoration to the origination, to affirm its possibility and His power over it.
2- The art of fronting (taqdīm): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «كَما بَدَأَكُمْ تَعُودُونَ», where He, glory be to Him, put what is compared to (al-mushabbah bihi) before what is compared (al-mushabbah), to alert the intelligent person that the determination of affairs never departs from the decree and the eternal knowledge.

* Benefits:
- Who devised the orthography (rasm) of the writing in the Quran?
The careful observer sees many words whose writing differs from the rules of writing we are accustomed to, such as «فحشة، الضللة، الشياطين», whose due was to be written «فاحشة، الضلالة، الشياطين» [Translator's note: the third word is printed identically in both lists in the source; the Quranic rasm intended is presumably «الشيطين» without the alif.]. Such cases are more than many in the orthography of the Noble Quran, and the right of this is to be studied and collected and a treatise written on it. We have come to know the stages of development of this language — its grammar and its dotting — and it grieves us that we have not found any reference giving a history for this reforming leap in the writing of our language, until this disparity arose between what we follow in spelling words today and what we find settled in the Noble Quran, which we feel reluctant to change or alter, out of reverence for this Book and to protect it from the tampering of those who tamper.

safi-cedvel:59-64.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام): the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath. (قد): a particle of verification (taḥqīq). (أرسلنا): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn ... and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of nominative, fāʿil (agent). (نوحا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (إلى قوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء): conjunctive. (قال): a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa". (يا): a vocative particle. (قوم): the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ, which was omitted for lightening ... and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (اعبدوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ما): a particle of negation. (اللام): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (من): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (إله): genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (غير): naʿt (adjective) of إله, following it in position, so it is nominative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إن): a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of inna. (أخاف): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anā". (على): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أخاف). (عذاب): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (يوم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (عظيم): naʿt of يوم, genitive.
The clause «أرسلنا....»: has no grammatical position, the reply to an implied oath ... and the oath clause is a resumption.
The clause «قال....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the reply to the oath.
The vocative clause «يا قوم....»: in the position of accusative, the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «اعبدوا....»: has no grammatical position, the reply to the vocative.
The clause «ما لكم من إله....»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إني أخاف عليكم ...»: has no grammatical position, causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أخاف عليكم ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
(60) (قال): like the first. (الملأ): fāʿil, nominative. (من قوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الملأ, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إنّا): like إني. (اللام): it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis. (نرى): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu", and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (في ضلال): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نراك). (مبين): naʿt of ضلال, genitive.
The clause «قال الملأ....»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «إنا لنراك ...»: in the position of accusative, the speech reported.
The clause «نراك....»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
(61) (قال): like the first. (يا قوم): like the first one. (ليس): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator — non-inflecting (jāmid). (الباء): a preposition, and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar of laysa. (ضلالة): the noun of laysa, postponed, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (لكن): a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator — for rectification (istidrāk), and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative, the noun of lākinna. (رسول): khabar, nominative. (من رب): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of رسول. (العالمين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «قال....»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «يا قوم ...»: in the position of accusative, the speech reported.
The clause «ليس بي ضلالة»: has no grammatical position, the reply to the vocative.
The clause «لكني رسول ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause of the reply to the vocative.
(62) (أبلغ): like أخاف, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (رسالات): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra. (رب): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive. (أنصح): like أخاف. (لكم): like عليكم, attached to (أنصح). (الواو): conjunctive. (أعلم): like أخاف. (من الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أعلم) [Note: It is permissible that it be attached to an omitted ḥāl of (ما) or of the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid), i.e. "I know what you do not know, it being from Allah".]. (ما): a relative noun [Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective, and the clause after it is in the position of accusative, a naʿt of it, and the referent pronoun is omitted.], in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (لا): a negating particle. (تعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «أبلغكم ...»: in the position of nominative, a second naʿt of رسول [Note: Or in the position of accusative, a ḥāl of رسول because it is qualified ... It is permissible that it be cut off as a resumption.].
The clause «أنصح لكم»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أبلغكم.
The clause «أعلم....»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أبلغكم.
The clause «تعلمون»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
(63) (الهمزة): for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī). (الواو): conjunctive. (عجبتم): like أرسلنا. (أن): a maṣdar-forming particle. (جاء): a past verb, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ذكر): fāʿil, nominative. (من رب): like the first, attached to a naʿt of ذكر, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (على رجل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a second naʿt of ذكر. (من): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a naʿt of رجل. (اللام): for causation (taʿlīl). (ينذر): an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو): conjunctive. (لتتقوا): like لينذر, and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءكم ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "min" ... attached to (عجبتم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ينذر) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جاءكم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تتقوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جاءكم), because it is conjoined to the maṣdar (أن ينذر).
(الواو): conjunctive. (لعلكم ترحمون): like لعلكم تذكرون [Note: In āya (57) of this sura.] ...
And the verb is passive, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «عجبتم....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined by the wāw to a resumed (mustaʾnafa) clause [Note: I.e.: "Have you denied and wondered that there came to you ...", and the resumed clause falls within the scope of the speech conveyed by Nūḥ, peace be upon him, to his people ... so the āya is an extension of the preceding āya.].
The clause «جاءكم ذكر»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first particle relative (أن).
The clause «ينذركم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle relative (أن).
The clause «تتقوا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third particle relative (أن).
The clause «لعلكم ترحمون»: has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «ترحمون»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of laʿalla.
(64) (الفاء): resumptive. (كذّبوا): a past verb and its fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الفاء): conjunctive. (أنجينا): like أرسلنا, and (الهاء) is like the preceding. (الواو): conjunctive. (الذين): a relative, in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object pronoun in (أنجيناه). (مع): an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted [verb of the] omitted ṣila, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (في الفلك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila. (الواو): conjunctive. (أغرقنا): like أرسلنا. (الذين): a relative, in the position of accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (كذبوا): like the first. (بآيات): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إنهم): like إني. (كانوا): a defective past verb — an abrogator — indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (قوما): the khabar of kāna, accusative. (عمين): naʿt of قوم, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «كذّبوه ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أنجيناه....»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive one.
The clause «أغرقنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أنجيناه.
The clause «كذّبوا بآياتنا»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «إنهم كانوا....»: has no grammatical position, causal.
The clause «كانوا قوما ...»: in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(رسالات): plural of رسالة, the noun from أرسل; it may be a non-derived (jāmid) noun denoting the thing sent. Its wazn is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ, and fatḥa is permissible.
(عمين): plural of عم, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from عمي يعمى, of the pattern (bāb) فرح; its wazn is فع with fatḥa on the fāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn. In عم there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by omission: the yāʾ was dropped from it because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) ... And in عمين there is also iʿlāl by omission: its original form is عميين with two yāʾs, the first with kasra and the second with sukūn; the first was dropped because the kasra on it is felt heavy, it being made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the mīm before it, and because of the meeting of two quiescents after that.

* Rhetoric:
- The non-metaphoric trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of the Exalted ﴿إِنَّا لَنَراكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ and His saying ﴿لَيْسَ بِي ضَلالَةٌ﴾: error has been made a container, while error is not a container in which a person dwells, because it is an abstract notion; it dwells only in its locus. So the use of error for its locus is a majāz mursal in which the state (ḥāl) is mentioned and the locus (maḥall) is meant; its relation is "stateness" (ḥāliyya), and its benefit is hyperbole in describing him with error and his being deeply sunk in it, as though he were settled in its darknesses, not budging from them.

* Benefits:
1- The scholars agree that the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) comes joined to «قد», in keeping with the emphasis of what is sworn upon. Exceptions to this rule are sayings that slipped from the tongues of their speakers and are not taken as a basis for analogy, such as the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
حلفت لها بالله حلفة فاجر ... لناموا فما إن من حديث ولا صال
(I swore to her by Allah the oath of a sinner: they have surely fallen asleep, so there is no one talking and no one warming himself at the fire.)
He ought to have said: «لقد ناموا», but he dropped قد in compliance with the soundness of the metre.
So reflect....!

safi-cedvel:158-158.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta". (يا): a vocative particle. (أيّ): the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper-noun-like vocative (mufrad ʿalam), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (الناس): a badal (substitute) of أيّ, following it in the nominative in form — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ. (رسول): the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ). (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (إلى): a preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive; attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رسول). (جميعا): a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the pronoun in إليكم. (الذي): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "huwa" [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, for praise; and it is permissible, weakly, for it to be a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty.]. (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive; attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (ملك): a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (السموات): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الواو) is a conjunction. (الأرض): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات, genitive. (لا): of generic negation. (إله): the noun of لا, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative. (إلّا): a particle of exception. (هو): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, a badal of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar, its implied form being "موجود" (existent) or "معبود بحقّ" (worshipped in truth) [Note: It may be a badal of the position of (لا إله), since its position is nominative, because it is originally a mubtadaʾ.]. (يحيي): an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa". (الواو): conjunction. (تميت): like يحيي. [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is يميت.] (الفاء): connective for the apodosis of an implied condition. (آمنوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn .. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا). (الواو): conjunction. (رسول): maʿṭūf to the Name of Majesty, genitive, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (النبيّ): a badal of رسول, genitive. (الأميّ): a naʿt of النبيّ, genitive. (الذي): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as a second naʿt of النبيّ [Note: It may be cut off for praise, so it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of a necessarily omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, or in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being أمدح (I praise).]. (يؤمن): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "huwa". (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمن). (الواو): conjunction. (كلمات): maʿṭūf to the Name of Majesty, genitive, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (اتّبعوا): like آمنوا, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (لعلّ): a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of لعلّ. (تهتدون): an imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The vocative clause with its answer: in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي رسول ...»: has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «(هو) الذي ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «له ملك السموات»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو»: has no grammatical position, a badal of the ṣila clause.
The clause «يحيي ...»: has no grammatical position, a badal of the clause لا إله إلّا هو.
The clause «يميت»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحيي.
The clause «آمنوا ...»: in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. إن أردتم الهداية والفوز بالجنّة فآمنوا ... (if you want guidance and the winning of the Garden, then believe ...) [Note: It is permissible for the fāʾ to be a conjunction linking the effect to the cause, and for the clause to be conjoined to the clause that answers the vocative: إنّي رسول اللَّه إليكم ...].
The clause «يؤمن بالله ...»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
The clause «اتّبعوه»: conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «لعلّكم تهتدون»: has no grammatical position, resumptive and causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تهتدون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:159-159.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (من قوم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). (موسى): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif, as it is a diptote. (أمّة): a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (يهدون): an imperfect verb, nominative .. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (بالحقّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يهدون, i.e. حال كونكم متلبّسين بالحقّ (in the state of your being clothed in the truth) [Translator's note: so in the source, «كونكم» (your being); the context requires «كونهم» (their being).]. (الواو): conjunction. (الباء): a preposition. (الهاء): a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يعدلون), which is like يهدون.
The clause «من قوم موسى أمّة»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يهدون ...»: in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أمّة.
The clause «يعدلون»: in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يهدون.

* Morphology:
(يهدون): in it there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is يهديون. The ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made vowelless and the dāl was given ḍamma — iʿlāl by making vowelless — then the yāʾ was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and it became يهدون. Its pattern is يفعون.

safi-cedvel:160-160.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (قطّعنا): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn ... and (نا) is a pronoun, fāʿil (agent), and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (اثنتي): a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), of the third-person pronoun in (قطّعناهم), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ [Note: If (قطّعنا) is made to imply the meaning of صيّرنا (We made into), then (اثنتي) is a second object.]. (عشرة): a numerical part with no grammatical position [Note: The word (عشرة) is put in the feminine because the omitted tamyīz (specification) is feminine, its implied form being فرقة (group) or أمّة (community).]. (أسباطا): a badal (substitute) of (اثنتي) عشرة, accusative like it. (أمما): a badal of (أسباط), accusative like it — or a naʿt (adjective) of it. (الواو): conjunction. (أوحينا): like قطّعنا. (إلى موسى): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحينا), the sign of the genitive being an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif. (إذ): an adverb of past time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (أوحينا). (استسقى): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (قوم): fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (أن): an explicative particle [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is governed by أوحينا through a preposition ...
and the clause اضرب is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.]. (اضرب): an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta". (بعصاك): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اضرب), the sign of the genitive being an implied kasra on the alif ... and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi. (الحجر): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الفاء): conjunction. (انبجس): a past verb, and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine. (من): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive; attached to (انبجست). (اثنتا): fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif, and the nūn is dropped because the compound resembles the construct. (عشرة): a numerical part with no grammatical position. (عينا): tamyīz, accusative. (قد): a particle of realisation. (علم): a past verb. (كلّ): fāʿil, nominative. (أناس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (مشرب): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (ظلّلنا): like قطّعنا. (على): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive; attached to (ظلّلنا). (الغمام): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو): conjunction. (أنزلنا ... المنّ): like ظلّلنا عليهم الغمام. (الواو): conjunction. (السلوى): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to المنّ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa on the alif. (كلوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil. (من طيّبات): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كلوا). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (رزقنا): like قطّعنا, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو): resumptive [Note: According to some it is a conjunction, conjoining the clause after it to an implied clause, i.e.: they wronged by their disbelief in those blessings, and they did not wrong Us by that.]. (ما): a negating particle. (ظلموا): a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو): conjunction. (لكن): a particle of rectification (istidrāk). (كانوا): an incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — and the wāw is its noun. (أنفس): a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يظلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative .. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قطّعناهم ...»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «أوحينا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «استسقاه قومه»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اضرب ...»: has no grammatical position, explicative.
The clause «انبجست ... اثنتا عشرة»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to an omitted resumptive clause, i.e. فضرب فانبجست (so he struck, and there gushed forth).
The clause «قد علم كلّ ...»: in the position of nominative as a naʿt of (اثنتا عشرة) عينا [Note: And the linking element is omitted, its implied form being منها (from them) ... or it has no grammatical position, resumptive, without supplying the linking element.].
The clause «ظلّلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قطّعناهم.
The clause «أنزلنا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ظلّلنا ...
The clause «كلوا ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of an implied saying (maqūl al-qawl), i.e.:
قلنا لهم كلوا (We said to them: eat).
The clause «رزقناكم»: has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما), and the referential pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e.: ما رزقناكم إيّاه or رزقناكموه.
The clause «ما ظلمونا»: has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «كانوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما ظلمونا.
The clause «يظلمون»: in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كانوا.

* Benefits:
1- The scholars stood up and sat down over the i'rab of «أسباطا», between its being a badal, a tamyīz and an adjective.
The view in which the soul finds rest, and which takes us out of the difficulties and objections, is that we make أسباطا an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being «اثنتي عشرة فرقة أسباطا» (twelve groups, as tribes).
2- The i'rab of the compound number from أحد عشر to تسعة عشر: it is parsed as «two compounded parts indeclinable on fatḥa, except اثني عشر, which is parsed with the i'rab of the dual.
As for the feminine and masculine of these compounds, they are divided, with respect to the first part, into two categories:
1- إحدى and اثنتا or ثنتا agree with the thing counted.
2- From ثلاث عشرة to تسع عشرة they differ from the thing counted. Remark: العشرة in the compound agrees with the thing counted in masculine and feminine, and when single it differs from the thing counted.

safi-cedvel:199-200.t:
* I'rab:
(خذ) imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is «you» (أنت); (العفو) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunctive; (أؤمر) like خذ [Translator's note: so spelled in the source, here and as (اومر) below; the Quranic word is وَأْمُرْ.]; (بالعرف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اومر), (الواو) conjunctive; (أعرض عن الجاهلين) like اومر بالعرف, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (أعرض), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «خذ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اومر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أعرض ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(الواو) conjunctive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (ما) a redundant (zāʾida) particle; (ينزغنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (النون) is for emphasis, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من الشيطان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينزغنّك) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of نزغ.], (نزغ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (استعذ بالله) like اومر بالعرف, and the preposition phrase is attached to (استعذ), (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of inna; (سميع) khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative; (عليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «ينزغنّك ... نزغ» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خذ.
The clause «استعذ ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنه سميع ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(العرف): a noun meaning what is recognised as good (al-maʿrūf) among things; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(نزغ): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb نزغ ينزغ, of the pattern فتح and of the pattern ضرب; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(استعذ): it contains a weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion, in keeping with being indeclinable on the sukūn; the ʿayn of the word was deleted in the imperative; its pattern is استفل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «خُذِ الْعَفْوَ», what is meant is «pardon them», since pardon is likened to a tangible thing that is sought and then taken.
2- The figure of smooth flow (fann al-insijām): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «خُذِ الْعَفْوَ» to the end of the verse. The Arabs greatly admired this verse for its ease of composition, sweetness of wording and soundness of construction, together with the far-reaching allusions and endless hints it contains. They gave this kind of style the name of a figure called «al-insijām» (smooth flow), which is that speech flows down like the flowing of streaming water, so that a sentence of prose or a verse of poetry has an effect on souls and an influence on hearts.

* Benefits:
«The inimitability of the Qur'an» 1- Lovers of eloquence admired the saying of Allah the Exalted «خُذِ الْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ الْجاهِلِينَ» for the inimitability and concision in it, and for the sweetness of its sound and the clarity of its expression;
and because it hints and does not explain, summarises and does not detail. The eloquent have ways in this kind of eloquence, and they named it «the figure of smooth flow» (fann al-insijām). Let us leave this figure, and let us draw our benefit from the subject of this verse, for it has been, and still is, the absorbing concern of the masters of ijtihād, since in His saying:
«خُذِ الْعَفْوَ» there is one of the principles of legislation in Islam, namely facilitation and not making things difficult. There are many indications on this matter, which people of judgment and ijtihād take up with verification and scrutiny.
In the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَأْمُرْ بِالْعُرْفِ» there is an explicit indication of taking custom (al-ʿurf) into account in legal rulings, and of respecting habit in dealings, as long as no explicit text of the Qur'an or the Hadith contradicts them.
On taking custom into account in the Law, and on adopting the removal of hardship from the Muslims, there is disagreement and long detail among the imams of ijtihād; whoever wishes, let him turn to the books of jurisprudence and its principles, for in them is quenching and cure for the burning, thirsty one.
As for the smooth flow in the verse, it prompts us to present these verses of Ṣafī al-Dīn for the extreme smooth flow in them:
قالت: كحلت الجفون بالوسن ... قلت: ارتقابا لطيفك الحسن
(She said: "You have lined your eyelids with slumber." I said: "Awaiting your lovely phantom.")

قالت: تسلّيت بعد فرقتنا ... قلت: عن مسكني وعن سكني
(She said: "You found consolation after our parting." I said: "For my dwelling and for my peace.")

قالت: تشاغلت عن محبتنا ... قلت بفرط البكاء والحزن
(She said: "You busied yourself away from our love." I said: "With excess of weeping and grief.")

قالت: تخلّيت، قلت: عن جلدي ... قالت: تغيّرت قلت في بدني
(She said: "You have given up." I said: "My endurance." She said: "You have changed." I said: "In my body.")
until he said:
انحلتني بالبعاد عنك فلو ... ترصدتني العيون لم ترني
(You have wasted me by distance from you, so that if eyes lay in wait for me they would not see me.)
It is said that one of the men of letters passed by the house of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī, after time had wronged it, taken away its splendour and worn out its finery, but the remains of its traces bore witness to its former bloom. He stood marvelling at the vicissitudes of time, quoting these verses:
ولقد وقفت على ربوعهم ... وطلولها بيد البلى نهب
(I stood at their dwellings, their ruins plundered by the hand of decay,)

فبكيت حتى ضحّ من لغب ... نضوي وعجّ بعذلي الركب
(and I wept until my lean camel groaned from weariness and the riders clamoured in reproach of me,)

وتلفّتت عيني فمذ خفيت ... عنّي الطلول تلفّت القلب
(and my eye kept turning back; and once the ruins were hidden from me, the heart turned back.)
Then a man passed by him and said: Do you know whose verses these are? He said: No. He said: By Allah, they are by the owner of this house. So we stood taking the lesson, and invoking mercy on the house and its owner ... Whoever is given to wonder, let him wonder at this coincidence.

safi-cedvel:201-203.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) like the previous [Note: In the previous verse (200).]; (الذين) a relative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as ism of inna; (اتّقوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إذا) an adverb for the future containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis تذكّروا or to its content, i.e. they gained insight after remembering; (مسّ) past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (طائف) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (من الشيطان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of طائف; (تذكّروا) like (اتّقوا); (الفاء) conjunctive; (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of the nominative; (مبصرون) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «إنّ الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّقوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «مسّهم طائف ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تذكّروا» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of inna.
The clause «هم مبصرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis clause.
(الواو) conjunctive; (إخوان) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: This pronoun refers to the devils, whose genus was mentioned in the previous verse with a singular word.], (يمدّون) imperfect verb, nominative ... and the wāw is the fāʿil [Note: The subject pronoun also refers to the devils.], (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi [Note: This pronoun refers to the disbelievers ... and the implied sense is: and the brothers of the devils – the devils extend them; and this attribution in the khabar runs onto someone other than the one to whom it belongs in meaning, for the extending is attributed to [Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.]], (في الغيّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يمدّون) [Note: This attachment is valid on the second interpretation – the view of Qatāda – if (في) is causal, i.e. because of their straying.. And the preposition phrase may be attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or the object, i.e. being, or settled, in error.], (ثمّ) a conjunction; (لا) negative; (يقصرون) imperfect verb like يمدّون.
The clause «إخوانهم يمدّونهم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إنّ الذين اتّقوا ...
The clause «يمدّونهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «لا يقصرون» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause يمدّونهم.
(الواو) conjunctive; (إذا) an adverb for the future containing the meaning of condition, attached to (قالوا), (لم) a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [to the past]; (تأت) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «you» (أنت); (بآية) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأت), (قالوا) like اتّقوا; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning هلّا («why not»); (اجتبيت) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn..
